hero.headline: Four arrested in Martin County after armed robbery of teen, pursuit
hero.body:
Four people accused in an armed robbery of a teenager were arrested in Martin County after a pursuit, according to deputies. The arrests occurred Monday following the incident involving the teenage victim.

Martin County deputies pursued the suspects before taking them into custody. The four individuals face charges related to the armed robbery.

The incident involved a teenage victim who was targeted in the armed robbery. Deputies did not immediately release the identities of the four arrested suspects.

The pursuit and arrests took place in Martin County on Monday. Further details about the robbery and chase were not immediately available from the Martin County Sheriff's Office.

cards.headline: United States seeks quarterfinal spot against Belgium with Balogun cleared to play
cards.teaser: The host United States is seeking to reach the World Cup quarterfinals for the first time since 2002 when it faces Belgium on Monday in Seattle with forward Folarin Balogun now cleared to play.
cards.body:
President Donald Trump intervened on behalf of American star forward Folarin Balogun, whose red-card suspension was lifted in a decision that allows him to play in a World Cup match against Belgium on Monday. Balogun, the American leader with three goals in the tournament, received a red card for stepping awkwardly on the right ankle of Tarik Muharemović of Bosnia-Herzegovina in a 2-0 round of 32 win on Wednesday, triggering an automatic one-game suspension. FIFA announced Sunday that the suspension had been lifted for the round of 16 match. Trump called FIFA president Gianni Infantino after the game asking FIFA review the red card, according to a person familiar with the call who spoke on condition of anonymity. Trump said in a statement on social media that FIFA did what was right and reversed a great injustice.

The host United States is seeking to reach the quarterfinals for the first time since 2002. The Americans lost in the round of 16 to Ghana in 2010, Belgium in 2014 and the Netherlands in 2022. They failed to advance from the group stage in 2006 and did not qualify for the 2018 tournament. American players learned of Balogun's availability when social media posts started popping up during the 10-minute bus ride Sunday morning from their hotel to training at the University of Washington's Husky Soccer Stadium, where they were greeted by Dubs II, the university's Alaskan Malamute. The U.S. Soccer Federation learned of FIFA's action in a message sent by FIFA in its portal at 10:31 a.m. EDT on Sunday.

cards.headline: St. Lucie Mets Snap Nine-Game Skid With Late Comeback Win Over Tarpons
cards.teaser:
The St. Lucie Mets ended their nine-game losing streak Sunday afternoon with a late offensive surge, rallying past the Tampa Tarpons for a 10-5 win at Clover Park.

St. Lucie trail
cards.body:
The St. Lucie Mets ended their nine-game losing streak Sunday afternoon with a late offensive surge, rallying past the Tampa Tarpons for a 10-5 win at Clover Park.

St. Lucie trailed 5-1 after six innings before scoring two runs in the seventh and seven more in the eighth to avoid a six-game sweep. Tampa had been trying to become the first team to sweep a six-game series against the Mets at Clover Park since Minor League Baseball adopted the format in 2021.

The decisive rally came in the eighth inning, when the Mets sent 13 batters to the plate and scored seven runs on four hits, three walks and two hit batters.

Catcher Francisco Toledo delivered the go-ahead hit with one out, ripping a two-run ground-rule double off Jordalin Mendoza to give St. Lucie a 6-5 lead. Taylor Darden followed with a two-run single against Parker Seay to extend the advantage to 8-5. Antonio Jimenez added an RBI infield single, and AJ Salgado drew a bases-loaded walk to cap the inning.

Tampa appeared in control earlier in the game. Engelth Urena homered in the fifth inning to stretch the Tarpons' lead to 5-1.

The Mets' first two runs came on solo home runs. Jimenez tied the game 1-1 in the first inning with his third homer of the season. Branny De Oleo added his sixth home run of the year in the seventh, cutting the deficit to 5-2.

St. Lucie kept the seventh-inning push going when Jeremy Rodriguez doubled and Jack Scanlon followed with an RBI double off Mendoza, bringing the Mets within 5-3.

Mets starter Emilio Obispo made his second appearance of the series and allowed one unearned run over three innings.

The bullpen kept St. Lucie within range after Calvin Ziegler allowed three runs in one-third of an inning during a MiLB rehab appearance. Justin Scarborough allowed only Urena's solo homer over 1.1 innings. Caden Wooster followed with 2.1 scoreless innings, and Ernesto Mercedes worked the final 1.2 innings without allowing a run to earn the win.

Jimenez led the Mets offensively, going 3-for-4 with a home run, three RBI and two runs scored. Rodriguez went 2-for-3 with a double and two runs, while Trey Snyder finished 2-for-4.

The Mets improved to 3-10 in the second half and 36-43 overall. They are off Monday before opening a six-game commuter series Tuesday against the Jupiter Hammerheads at Roger Dean Chevrolet Stadium. First pitch is scheduled for 6:30 p.m.

cards.headline: Peacock House Art Foundation transforms Fort Pierce into artistic destination with history and global artists
cards.teaser: The Peacock House Art Foundation is transforming Fort Pierce into an artistic destination, putting the Peacock Arts District on the map and connecting local and international artists at the historic Crain Estate.
cards.body:
The Peacock House Art Foundation preserves the legacy of Jaxson and Mary Crain at the historic Crain Estate in Fort Pierce. Jaxson Crain was a tile worker by trade, and his craftsmanship is visible throughout the entire facility from the ground to the walls to the ceiling. Krystal Masters, the art director, said the estate is 90% the way it was when the Crains were there. The house retains original features including the smoking and bourbon room with man paneling, manly bathroom colors, pre-stained glass, and a bar on the front patio. Visitors can take guided tours of the lush gardens and vibrant architecture every Monday, Wednesday, and Friday. The couple traveled the world nine times, collecting one-of-a-kind items for their Florida estate including a gazebo shipped from India that features tiny peacocks. The foundation has made a conscious effort to preserve the estate's original character and avoid commercialization.

The Peacock House gets its name from the birds that have roamed the property for decades. The Crains are believed to have introduced peacocks to Fort Pierce in the 1970s, bringing in seven originally that have grown to over 100. Among the flock is a beloved bird named Bob, believed to be 60 years old, who walks with a limp and is hand-fed daily from his own bowls. The foundation's artist-in-residency program attracts artists from around the world, housing them in simple but elegant accommodations on the property. The art lab offers classes for children and adults of all skill levels. Masters leads one-on-one classes where students with zero experience walk out with a piece of art. Classes include sculpting and workshops like paint your pet in watercolor and rainbow.

cards.headline: 40-year-old driver killed in head-on crash on State Road 710 in Martin County
cards.body:
A 40-year-old man was killed early Sunday after a head-on crash on State Road 710 in Martin County, according to the Florida Highway Patrol. The crash happened around 2 a.m. near State Road 710, also known as Beeline Highway, and Southwest Silver Fox Lane. FHP said a 2015 Kia Optima was traveling north on State Road 710 when the driver crossed into the southbound lane and collided head-on with a 2021 Toyota Tundra. The front left of the Kia struck the front left of the Tundra. Upon impact, the Kia burst into flames and came to rest on the grass shoulder facing north. The Tundra came to rest facing southeast in the southbound lane. The driver of the Kia, a 40-year-old man, died at the scene. The driver of the Tundra, a 41-year-old man from Indiantown, was taken to the hospital via LifeStar medical helicopter.

Martin County Fire Rescue has responded to 42 vehicle accident-related calls on State Road 710 just this year. After a fatal crash in January, Martin County Sheriff John Budensiek called the road a "death trap." Bill Townsend, who lives nearby, said the road has long been a concern for residents. "People don't pay a whole lot of attention to other people on the road, and [it's] kind of a dangerous road sometimes," Townsend said. "Everybody's always in a hurry... just living here makes me worry about the young people learning to drive and learning to drive on that road concerns me, because I have young kids."

The Florida Department of Transportation has plans to widen the road from two lanes to four, but construction is not expected to begin until 2031. "The question will be how many more people have to die before we get that project going. Florida touts that they have the safest roads in the country but this road is one that clearly is not in that category," Budensiek said in January. In the meantime, FDOT has begun improvements to the road, including pavement, markings, signage and new turn lanes.

Townsend said faster action is needed. "It would be beneficial to the people that live and travel that road all the time if something happened faster," Townsend said.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie works to expand Midway Road, add partial Florida Turnpike interchange
cards.teaser: Port St. Lucie City Council last month approved the first reading of an ordinance to give 7 acres of land to the Florida Department of Transportation to assist with a partial interchange coming to Florida's Turnpike in St. Lucie County.
cards.body:
Port St. Lucie City Council last month approved the first reading of an ordinance to give 7 acres of land to the Florida Department of Transportation to assist with a partial interchange coming to Florida's Turnpike. Scott Samples, strategic communications manager for Port St. Lucie, said the interchange addresses a significant gap between entrances and exits to the Turnpike currently in Port St. Lucie and is designed to accommodate growth that's already occurred and will occur over the next 20 to 50 years.

FDOT has been constructing the $95 million Midway Road Widening Project to help with congestion and safety. Crews are currently working on the first phase widening the road from two lanes to four lanes from Selvitz Road to Jenkins Road. The second widening phase from Jenkins Road to Glades Cut Off Road is still in the design phase and construction is anticipated to begin in Summer 2027.

FDOT is also working on improving the Turnpike bridge and adding a partial interchange for the Turnpike, which is still in the design phase. The Midway Road Widening Project will also add bike and pedestrian paths along with sidewalks. City council will vote on final approval to give the land at an upcoming meeting.

cards.headline: Hobe Sound community rallies around man who lost fiance in deadly home fire
cards.teaser: A Hobe Sound man is leaning on his community after losing his fiance Misty Dawn White, 46, who was found dead Monday after a fire broke out inside the couple's home.
cards.body:
Misty Dawn White, 46, was found dead Monday after a fire broke out inside the couple's Hobe Sound home. Preliminary findings from the sheriff's office point to an electrical issue as a possible cause. The fire remains under investigation.

Nina Fenn, a friend of White's for eight years, said she received a call from White's fiancé Mark stating that Misty had passed away in a fire. Friends have since launched a fundraiser to help Mark rebuild after the flames destroyed many of his and White's belongings. Fenn said Mark lost his one and only child, Jacob, tragically. Fenn said White was a Christian woman who loved gardening and plants and played the piano. She loved kids and people and was always the first to lend a hand. White's birthday is the Fourth of July, so she passed just a few days before her birthday, Fenn said.

cards.headline: St. Lucie County marine deputies rescue 2 after boat sinks in Intracoastal Waterway
cards.teaser: St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office Marine Unit rescued two boaters after their small motorized boat took on water and became submerged in the Intracoastal Waterway on July 1.
cards.body:
The St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office Marine Unit responded to reports of a small motorized boat taking on water and becoming submerged in the Intracoastal Waterway on July 1. Body-worn camera footage captured the rescue as it unfolded. Both occupants ended up in the water when their boat went down, but deputies say they were wearing life jackets that kept them afloat while help arrived.

Marine Unit deputies quickly located the pair in the water and safely brought them aboard their patrol vessel. The boaters were then transported back to the boat ramp without any injuries reported. "This incident serves as an important reminder that wearing a life jacket can save your life," the sheriff's office said in a Facebook post. "We're grateful this call ended safely and proud of the swift response by our Marine Unit deputies who are always ready to answer the call."

cards.headline: Stuart downtown dock closes Monday for $3 million renovation that will nearly double slip capacity
cards.body:
Stuart's downtown public dock will close July 6 for a $3 million renovation projected to be complete by next Fourth of July. The project will nearly double the dock's capacity, expanding from 18 to 44 slips for both motorized and non-motorized vessels. The renovation is funded by a state grant and transportation impact fees and will include a 7,500 square foot fixed dock, a 1,400 square foot floating dock and a smaller floating platform. More than 1,400 boaters use the dock annually. Mayor Sean Reed said the upgrades are designed to prevent storm damage during hurricanes and major storms. Boat captain Parker Fisher said the dock has needed work over the years and expressed hope for more floating docks to be added.

During the closure, the city is working to accommodate businesses and boaters who rely on the dock for drop-off and pick-up. Tiki Taxi & Cruises, which operates off the dock, initially had concerns about whether it could continue running during construction. Austin Kuyrkendall, director of operations for Tiki Taxi & Cruises, said the city found a solution by allowing the company to build a gate at the end of the non-floating section of the downtown Stuart dock for boarding passengers. Kuyrkendall said Stuart is not Stuart without the water and acknowledged the dock's current limitations become apparent on weekends when vessels squeeze in to find spots. He said modernizing and expanding the dock will be great for the city and his business.

hero.headline: Serena Williams withdraws from Wimbledon doubles with sister Venus due to knee injury
hero.teaser: Serena Williams pulled out of her doubles match with sister Venus at Wimbledon on Saturday after a right knee injury sustained during her singles return earlier in the week.
hero.body:
Serena Williams withdrew from her doubles match with sister Venus at Wimbledon on Saturday due to a right knee injury. The 44-year-old was injured during her singles return earlier in the week in a three-set loss. She posted on Instagram that she was heartbroken to withdraw and that the opportunity to play alongside Venus Williams once more meant the world to her. She said she did everything she could but her knee is not ready to compete. The post included images of four syringes showing fluid drained from her knee after her singles match. An accompanying video showed her walking with strapping up and down her right leg and what appeared to be one of her daughters holding a cane for her. Serena was beaten 6-3, 6-7 (6), 6-3 by 20-year-old Maya Joint of Australia on Tuesday.

The Williams sisters were scheduled to play Camila Osorio and Solana Sierra. It was the only first-round doubles match that wasn't scheduled earlier in the week, having been pushed back to give Serena more time to recover. With the U.S. Open approaching, Serena indicated she could play again somewhere else soon, telling followers to stay tuned to a city near you. Venus, 46, played in the mixed doubles tournament on Friday with Kevin Krawietz, losing in straight sets to Tereza Mihalikova and Lloyd Glasspool. The Williams sisters are six-time champions as partners in women's doubles at Wimbledon.

cards.headline: Argentina beats Cape Verde 3-2 in extra time to advance to World Cup Round of 16
cards.teaser: Lionel Messi and Argentina survived a scare from Cape Verde in a thrilling match that went to extra time before the defending World Cup champion advanced to face Egypt.
cards.body:
Argentina beat Cape Verde 3-2 on Friday and advanced to the World Cup Round of 16 in a match where the tiny island nation challenged the reigning champion until the final minutes of extra time. The go-ahead score for Argentina was credited as an own-goal after Cristian Romero's header deflected off Cape Verde's Diney Borges in the 111th minute. Lisandro Martinez scored in the 103rd minute to put Argentina ahead 2-1.

Messi scored early in regulation for his record-extending 20th career World Cup goal. Sidny Lopes Cabral and Deroy Duarte scored for Cape Verde, both equalizers that stunned the pro-Argentina crowd in South Florida. Cape Verde goalkeeper Vozinha, 40, had 10 saves against Argentina, including five against Messi.

Argentina will face Egypt in Atlanta on Tuesday. Messi has seven goals in this tournament, one more than France's Kylian Mbappé in the Golden Boot race as the top scorer. He extended his World Cup record to 12 goals during his record eight-match scoring streak. Cape Verde became the smallest country to reach the knockout round after securing draws against Spain, Uruguay and Saudi Arabia.

cards.headline: Saint Andrew's Scots football targets state title after 10-2 season and district championship
cards.body:
The Saint Andrew's Scots finished last season with a 10-2 record and a district title, but a second-round playoff exit left the team wanting more as they prepare for the 2026 fall football season. Head football coach Jimmy Robertson said most of the seniors are four-year seniors, with the majority coming from the middle school. The program has scheduled more challenging opponents this fall as part of its strategy to compete at a higher level.

Senior Jack Williams said the team wanted to take the program to the next level by playing against really good teams to attract new people. Senior Jack Whelche said a better year means going farther in the playoffs, noting that going undefeated in the season does not matter if they keep losing in the second round. Senior Edmyer St. Jean said the daily summer workouts add up as something to look forward to, allowing them to work harder so they can see positive results when the season ends. The veteran senior class is leading the way as the Scots set their sights on a state title.

hero.headline: Storm Chances Remain Across Florida Today Before Drier Pattern Moves In
hero.body:
Florida faces continued storm chances today before a shift to lower rain probabilities later in the week, according to forecasters. The state remains under active weather conditions with thunderstorm potential across multiple regions, though the daily pattern of afternoon storms is expected to ease as the week progresses.

South Florida will experience steamy conditions to start the workweek with chances of showers and storms throughout the area. The combination of heat and humidity creates the typical summer weather pattern that residents have experienced in recent weeks. Morning conditions set the stage for storm development as temperatures rise throughout the day and atmospheric moisture remains elevated across the region.

The forecast calls for lower storm chances beginning later in the week, offering residents a break from the daily thunderstorm routine. Meteorologists indicate this drier pattern should hold for much of the remainder of the week, representing a shift from the consistent storm activity that has characterized recent days. While the overall trend points toward decreased rainfall, isolated showers remain possible as summer weather patterns continue to dominate across the Florida peninsula. The change comes as atmospheric conditions modify slightly, reducing the ingredients necessary for widespread thunderstorm development that has been occurring regularly.

Today's storm potential marks the final day of heightened activity before the transition to calmer conditions takes hold. The shift to a drier weather pattern will provide relief for outdoor activities and events that have been impacted by daily afternoon and evening thunderstorms. Forecasters emphasize that while storm chances decrease significantly after today, Florida's summer weather remains inherently variable, and residents should continue monitoring local conditions. The state's position and summer climate mean that even during drier patterns, localized storm development remains possible when conditions align. As the week progresses, the focus shifts from managing daily storm threats to enjoying more stable weather conditions across most of Florida.

hero.headline: Four arrested in Martin County after armed robbery of teen, pursuit
hero.body:
Four people accused in an armed robbery of a teenager were arrested in Martin County after a pursuit, according to deputies. The arrests occurred Monday following the incident involving the teenage victim.

Martin County deputies pursued the suspects before taking them into custody. The four individuals face charges related to the armed robbery.

The incident involved a teenage victim who was targeted in the armed robbery. Deputies did not immediately release the identities of the four arrested suspects.

The pursuit and arrests took place in Martin County on Monday. Further details about the robbery and chase were not immediately available from the Martin County Sheriff's Office.
